work: Enarratio in Epistolam B. Pauli ad Hebræos
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

6.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI SEXTI : QUAPROPTER INTERMITTENTES, ETC.
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: Wherefore, leaving, etc.

paras.t: Posita increpatione Hebræorum, subjungitur blanda exhortatio eorumdem. Quapropter, videlicet quoniam perfectorum est solidus cibus, intermittentes inchoationis Christi sermonem, id est prima atque communia christianæ doctrinæ principia, ut sunt articuli fidei, ad perfectionem, id est ad veram sapientiam et sanctam conversationem, feramur, id est moveamur, Deo per gratiam nos intus excitante, et proximo adjuvante, vel anima se ipsam hortante. Consequenter ostendit Apostolus quæ sunt quæ velit jam prætermittere, eo quod spectent ad inchoationem sermonis Christi, tanquam fidei rudimenta quibus novelli in fide instrui habent. Sunt autem sex, sicut patebit. Non rursum jacientes fundamentum pœnitentiæ, id est non iterum tractantes de sacramento Pœnitentiæ, quæ est primum fundamentum quantum ad peccatores adultos baptizatos, gratiam adipisci conantes : quæ pœnitentia est ab operibus mortuis, id est recessus ac dolor de peccatis, quæ interficiunt animam. Nec rursus jacientes fundamentum fidei ad Deum, id est, non iterum de ipsa fide, quæ est fundamentum virtutum, loquentes, videlicet de nuda ac simplici fide. Infra tamen fit sermo prolixus de fide idonea atque perfecta.
paras.en: Having set down his rebuke of the Hebrews, he adds a gentle exhortation to them. [[6:1|Wherefore|Quapropter]], namely, since strong meat is for the perfect, [[6:1|leaving the word of the beginning of Christ|intermittentes inchoationis Christi sermonem]], that is, the first and common principles of Christian doctrine, such as the articles of faith, to perfection [Denis reads *ad perfectionem* where the Vulgate has *ad perfectiora*], that is, to true wisdom and holy conversation, [[6:1|let us go on|feramur]], that is, let us be moved, God stirring us inwardly by grace, and our neighbour helping, or the soul exhorting itself. Next the Apostle shows what the things are which he now wishes to pass over, because they belong to the beginning of the word of Christ, as the rudiments of faith in which the newly converted are to be instructed. And they are six, as will appear. [[6:1|not laying again the foundation of penance|Non rursum jacientes fundamentum pœnitentiæ]], that is, not treating again of the sacrament of Penance, which is the first foundation for adult baptized sinners striving to obtain grace: which penance is [[6:1|from dead works|ab operibus mortuis]], that is, a withdrawal from and sorrow for sins, which kill the soul. Nor again laying the foundation [[6:1|of faith towards God|fidei ad Deum]], that is, not speaking again of faith itself, which is the foundation of the virtues, namely of bare and simple faith. Below, however, a lengthy discourse is made of fitting and perfect faith.

paras.t: Baptismatum doctrinæ, id est non denuo determinantes de Baptismo christianæ legis. Dicit autem pluraliter, Baptismatum, propter triplex Baptisma, videlicet fluminis, flaminis et sanguinis. Impositionis quoque manuum, id est, non iterum tractantes de sacramento Confirmationis, in quo datur Spiritus Sanctus ac robur animæ per impositionem manuum. Ac resurrectionis mortuorum, id est, non de generali mortuorum resurrectione rursus agentes. Et judicii æterni, id est, non de finali judicio denuo pertractantes : quod ideo appellatur æternum, quia effectus sententiæ Judicis, scilicet merces reddenda, æternaliter durat. Et hoc faciemus, id est, prædicto modo procedemus, faciliora prætermittendo et ad perfectionem tendendo, si quidem permiserit Deus, id est, si tempus vivendi, gratiamque adimplendi præstiterit.
paras.en: [[6:2|Of the doctrine of baptisms|Baptismatum doctrinæ]], that is, not determining anew concerning the Baptism of the Christian law. He says *baptisms* in the plural because of the threefold Baptism, namely of water, of the Spirit and of blood [Latin *fluminis, flaminis et sanguinis*, a jingle: of the stream, of the breath, of blood]. [[6:2|and imposition of hands|Impositionis quoque manuum]], that is, not treating again of the sacrament of Confirmation, in which the Holy Ghost and strength of soul are given by the imposition of hands. [[6:2|and of the resurrection of the dead|Ac resurrectionis mortuorum]], that is, not dealing again with the general resurrection of the dead. [[6:2|and of eternal judgment|Et judicii æterni]], that is, not treating anew of the final judgment, which is called eternal because the effect of the Judge's sentence, namely the reward to be rendered, endures eternally. [[6:3|And this will we do|Et hoc faciemus]], that is, we shall proceed in the said manner, passing over the easier things and tending to perfection, [[6:3|if God permit|si quidem permiserit Deus]], that is, if He grant time to live and grace to fulfil it.

paras.t: Impossibile est enim, eos, etc. Hoc tribus modis exponitur. Primo sic : Ad perfectionem feramur, nec opinemur nos posse per Baptismum sæpius emundari. Impossibile est enim, eos qui semel sunt illuminati, id est, fidem et gratiam primo receperunt in fonte Baptismatis, et gustaverunt donum cœleste, id est, divinæ pietatis effectum, videlicet peccatorum remissionem et consolationem internam, experti sunt, et participes facti sunt Spiritus Sancti, id est, septem dona Spiritus Sancti sortiti sunt : quæ omnia simul cum gratia gratum faciente infunduntur, et simul cum ea habentur atque perduntur ; gustaverunt nihilo minus bonum Dei verbum, id est, Christi dulcedinem secundum ejus divinitatem contemplando ac diligendo senserunt : de quo verbo Pater testatur, Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum ; vel, Bonum Dei verbum, id est evangelicæ doctrinæ sermonem, ita ut dicere valeant : Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua ! Illud quoque Jeremiæ : Factus est sermo Domini in corde meo quasi ignis exæstuans, claususque in ossibus meis ; et defeci, ferre non sustinens ; virtutesque sæculi venturi, id est, cœlestes perfectiones, seu animæ et corporis dotes in patria habendas jam gustaverunt per spem seu aliquam prælibationem ac inchoationem : et prolapsi sunt, id est, post tanta beneficia in vitia corruerunt : renovari rursus, id est spiritualiter regenerari, ad pœnitentiam, id est ad gratiam pœnitendi, videlicet ut gratiam reparent per Baptismum, rursum crucifigentes sibimetipsis Filium Dei, id est, isti qui per Baptismi iterationem resurgere putant a culpis, iterum, quantum in ipsis est, et ad propriam damnationem, crucifigunt Christum, et ostentui habentes, id est, eum irrident. Nam et crucifixoribus et irrisoribus Christi consimiles sunt. Quum enim in Baptismo configurentur Christo passo atque sepulto (juxta quod dictum est ad Romanos : Quicumque baptizati sumus in Christo Jesu, in morte ipsius baptizati sumus ; consepulti enim sumus cum illo per Baptismum, etc.), dum ergo asserunt Baptismum iterari posse, passionem quoque ipsius iterabilem fore protestari videntur.
paras.en: [[6:4|For it is impossible for those|Impossibile est enim, eos]], etc. This is expounded in three ways. First thus: Let us go on to perfection, and let us not suppose that we can be cleansed more than once by Baptism. [[6:4|For it is impossible for those who were once illuminated|Impossibile est enim, eos qui semel sunt illuminati]], that is, who first received faith and grace in the font of Baptism, [[6:4|have tasted also the heavenly gift|et gustaverunt donum cœleste]], that is, have experienced the effect of divine mercy, namely the remission of sins and inward consolation, [[6:4|and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost|et participes facti sunt Spiritus Sancti]], that is, have received the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]][[Is 11:3||]], all of which are infused together with sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God], and are had and lost together with it; [[6:5|Have moreover tasted the good word of God|gustaverunt nihilo minus bonum Dei verbum]], that is, have felt the sweetness of Christ according to His divinity by contemplating and loving Him: of which Word the Father testifies, [[Ps 44:2|My heart hath uttered a good word|Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum]]; or, the good word of God, that is, the discourse of the gospel teaching, so that they can say: [[Ps 118:103|How sweet are thy words to my palate!|Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua]]! And that of Jeremias: [[Jer 20:9|and there came in my heart as a burning fire, shut up in my bones, and I was wearied, not being able to bear it|Factus est sermo Domini in corde meo quasi ignis exæstuans, claususque in ossibus meis ; et defeci, ferre non sustinens]]; [[6:5|and the powers of the world to come|virtutesque sæculi venturi]], that is, have already tasted, by hope or some foretaste and beginning, the heavenly perfections, or the endowments of soul and body to be had in the fatherland: [[6:6|And are fallen away|et prolapsi sunt]], that is, after such great benefits have fallen headlong into vices: [[6:6|to be renewed again|renovari rursus]], that is, to be spiritually regenerated, [[6:6|to penance|ad pœnitentiam]], that is, to the grace of repenting, namely so as to recover grace by Baptism, [[6:6|crucifying again to themselves the Son of God|rursum crucifigentes sibimetipsis Filium Dei]], that is, those who think to rise from their sins by repeating Baptism crucify Christ again, as far as in them lies, and to their own damnation, [[6:6|and making him a mockery|et ostentui habentes]], that is, they mock Him. For they are like those who crucified and mocked Christ. Since in Baptism they are conformed to Christ who suffered and was buried (according to what is said to the Romans: [[Rom 6:3|all we who are baptized in Christ Jesus are baptized in his death?|Quicumque baptizati sumus in Christo Jesu, in morte ipsius baptizati sumus]]; [[Rom 6:4|For we are buried together with him by baptism into death|consepulti enim sumus cum illo per Baptismum]], etc.), when therefore they assert that Baptism can be repeated, they seem to declare that His passion too can be repeated.

paras.t: Secundo, exponitur de quocumque recidivante, qui post prædicta beneficia in magna peccata prolabitur, et in iis quodammodo habituatur. Non enim homo prædictas gratias experitur, nisi sit valde perfectus. Talis vero non subito evacuatur, sed paulatim, donec penitus obtenebretur. Tales ergo ad pœnitentiam renovari, id est iterum emendari et pœnitere, impossibile est, id est difficile. Secundum quem modum peccata in Spiritum Sanctum dicuntur irremissibilia. Et Christus Judæis dixit : Quomodo potestis loqui bona, quum sitis mali? Sic enim apud Prophetam legitur : Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam, et vos poteritis bene facere. Hujusmodi quoque iterum crucifigunt sibi Filium Dei, quoniam quantum in ipsis est, causam suæ crucifixionis reiterant. — Tertio, exponitur pro statu futuri sæculi, ut sit sensus, quod prædicti renovari non possunt ad pœnitentiam post hanc vitam, secundum quod scriptum est : Venit nox quando nemo potest operari.
paras.en: Secondly, it is expounded of any backslider who, after the said benefits, falls into great sins and becomes in a manner habituated to them. For a man does not experience the said graces unless he is very perfect. Such a one is not emptied out suddenly, but little by little, until he is wholly darkened. For such, then, to be renewed to penance, that is, to amend and repent again, is *impossible*, that is, difficult. In this sense sins against the Holy Ghost are said to be unforgivable. And Christ said to the Jews: [[Matt 12:34|how can you speak good things, whereas you are evil?|Quomodo potestis loqui bona, quum sitis mali]]? For so we read in the Prophet: [[Jer 13:23|If the Ethiopian can change his skin|Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam]], you also may do well. Such men too crucify again to themselves the Son of God, since, as far as in them lies, they repeat the cause of His crucifixion. — Thirdly, it is expounded of the state of the world to come, so that the sense is that the said persons cannot be renewed to penance after this life, according to what is written: [[John 9:4|the night cometh, when no man can work|Venit nox quando nemo potest operari]].

paras.t: Primus autem intellectus convenientior est. Apostolus enim loquitur Hebræis, amputans eis occasionem errandi circa Baptismum, videlicet ne sic arbitrarentur repeti posse Baptismatis sacramentum, quemadmodum ablutiones et baptismata legis Moysis iterabantur.
paras.en: The first interpretation, however, is the more fitting. For the Apostle is speaking to Hebrews, cutting off from them occasion of error about Baptism, namely lest they should think the sacrament of Baptism could be repeated in the way the washings and baptisms of the law of Moses were repeated.

paras.t: Denique, ex præinductis verbis Apostoli Novatius, Romanæ Ecclesiæ diaconus, sumpsit occasionem hæreticæ impietatis, affirmans sacramentum Pœnitentiæ iterari non posse. Ad cujus erroris confirmationem aliqui adduxerunt quod scriptum est in Job : Ecce hæc tribus vicibus operatur Deus per singulos. Et in libro Regum : Si peccaverit vir in virum, placari ei potest Deus ; si autem in Deum peccaverit, quis exorabit pro eo? Et multa similia in Scripturis habentur, ut quum ait Joannes : Est peccatum ad mortem ; non dico ut pro illo quis oret. Quæ omnia prudenti indigent intellectu, ne verba vitæ et veritatis fiant pabula mortis et falsitatis.
paras.en: Finally, from the aforesaid words of the Apostle Novatius, a deacon of the Roman Church, took occasion for his heretical impiety, affirming that the sacrament of Penance cannot be repeated. In confirmation of this error some adduced what is written in Job: [[Job 33:29|Behold, all these things God worketh three times within every one|Ecce hæc tribus vicibus operatur Deus per singulos]] [Denis's Latin reads literally “three times”]. And in the book of Kings: [[1 Kings 2:25|If one man shall sin against another, God may be appeased in his behalf: but if a man shall sin against the Lord, who shall pray for him?|Si peccaverit vir in virum, placari ei potest Deus ; si autem in Deum peccaverit, quis exorabit pro eo?]]? And many similar things are found in the Scriptures, as when John says: [[1 John 5:16|There is a sin unto death. For that I say not that|Est peccatum ad mortem ; non dico ut pro illo quis oret]]. All of which need prudent understanding, lest the words of life and truth become the food of death and falsehood.

paras.t: Præterea, quod prædicto modo recidivantes, vel rebaptizari volentes, non renoventur ad pœnitentiam, secundum expositiones prætactas, ostendit per simile. Terra enim sæpe venientem super se bibens imbrem, id est, humorem seu pluviam sibi desuper incidentem consumens, et generans herbam opportunam, id est fructum convenientem, illis a quibus colitur mediate et immediate, id est agricolis, seu possessoribus qui eam faciunt arari et exerceri ; accipit benedictionem a Deo, id est, Deo eam fecundante, a suis cultoribus commendatur tanquam fructifera; vel, Accipit benedictionem, id est fecunditatem a Deo, tanquam a prima principalique causa. Proferens autem spinas et tribulos, id est infructuosa exsistens, reproba est et maledicto proxima, id est, reprobatur et tanquam sterilis maledicitur; cujus consummatio, id est fructificatio, scilicet spinarum ac tribulorum productio, erit in combustionem, id est, igni tradetur. — Spiritualiter terra ista est homo, cujus anima accipit imbrem super se venientem, id est cœlestis gratiæ vel sapientiæ salutaris profluvium. Quum autem producit herbam opportunam, id est opera virtuosa, convenientia illis a quibus colitur, id est angelis custodibus et prælatis ac prædicatoribus, accipit benedictionem, id est gratiæ incrementum, a Deo. Habenti enim dabitur, et abundabit. Proferens autem spinas et tribulos, id est passiones acutas et opera prava, reproba est : cujus consummatio, id est finis, erit in combustionem ignis æterni, prout Salvator ait : Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras sicut palmes, et colligent eum, et in ignem mittent.
paras.en: Further, he shows by a likeness that those who relapse in the said way, or wish to be rebaptized, are not renewed to penance, according to the expositions given above. [[6:7|For the earth, that drinketh in the rain which cometh often upon it|Terra enim sæpe venientem super se bibens imbrem]], that is, consuming the moisture or rain falling on it from above, [[6:7|and bringeth forth herbs meet|et generans herbam opportunam]], that is, fitting fruit, [[6:7|for them by whom it is tilled|illis a quibus colitur]] mediately and immediately, that is, for the husbandmen, or the owners who have it ploughed and worked; [[6:7|receiveth blessing from God|accipit benedictionem a Deo]], that is, God making it fruitful, it is praised by its tillers as fruitful; or, *receiveth blessing*, that is, fruitfulness from God, as from the first and principal cause. [[6:8|But that which bringeth forth thorns and briers|Proferens autem spinas et tribulos]], that is, being unfruitful, [[6:8|is reprobate and very near unto a curse|reproba est et maledicto proxima]], that is, it is rejected and cursed as barren; [[6:8|whose end|cujus consummatio]], that is, its fruiting, namely the production of thorns and briers, [[6:8|is to be burnt|in combustionem]], that is, it will be given to the fire. — Spiritually this earth is man, whose soul receives the rain coming upon it, that is, the outpouring of heavenly grace or saving wisdom. And when it brings forth fit herbs, that is, virtuous works, fitting for those by whom it is tilled, that is, the guardian angels and prelates and preachers, it receives blessing, that is, increase of grace, from God. For [[Matt 25:29|to every one that hath shall be given, and he shall abound|Habenti enim dabitur, et abundabit]]. But bringing forth thorns and briers, that is, sharp passions and wicked works, it is reprobate: whose end will be the burning of eternal fire, as the Saviour says: [[John 15:6|If any one abide not in me, he shall be cast forth as a branch and shall wither: and they shall gather him up and cast him into the fire|Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras sicut palmes, et colligent eum, et in ignem mittent]].

paras.t: Sed ne propter præinductæ increpationis rigorem exasperarentur, vel pusillanimes fierent, consequenter adjungit blandam consolationem. Confidimus autem de vobis, dilectissimi, meliora et viciniora saluti, id est, perfectiora opera et beatitudinis magis meritoria, vobis inesse speramus, quam superius insinuasse videmur, vel quam sint spinæ ac tribuli quæ suffocant verbum Dei ; tametsi ita loquimur, id est, quamvis tam dure vos increpavimus. Et rationabiliter ita confidimus : Non enim injustus est Deus, cujus virtus justitiæ initium est, ut obliviscatur operis vestri, id est, per modum obliviscentis se habeat, non attendendo nec remunerando vestra opera bona, et dilectionis Dei ac proximi, quam intus latentem, ostendistis foris per actus caritativos (nam exhibitio operis, probatio est caritatis : ideo dicit quoque Salvator, Si quis diligit me, sermones meos servabit), in nomine ipsius, id est propter amorem Dei et gloriam ejus ; quia ministrastis, id est, necessaria vitæ præbuistis et obsequia congrua impendistis, sanctis, id est fide et opere christianis, et ministratis eis, perseverando in opere inchoato : sicut et ad Galatas jam dictum est : Per caritatem servite invicem.
paras.en: But lest they be embittered or grow faint-hearted because of the severity of the foregoing rebuke, he next adds a gentle consolation. [[6:9|But, my dearly beloved, we trust better things of you, and nearer to salvation|Confidimus autem de vobis, dilectissimi, meliora et viciniora saluti]], that is, we hope that there are in you works more perfect and more meritorious of beatitude than we seemed to hint above, or than the thorns and briers which choke the word of God[[Luke 8:7||]][[Luke 8:14||]] [the margin prints Luc. xiii, 7, 14; the parable of the sower is Luke 8:7, 14]; [[6:9|though we speak thus|tametsi ita loquimur]], that is, although we have rebuked you so harshly. And with reason we so trust: [[6:10|For God is not unjust|Non enim injustus est Deus]], whose power is the beginning of justice[[Wis 12:16||]], [[6:10|that he should forget your work|ut obliviscatur operis vestri]], that is, that He should behave as one forgetting, not heeding nor rewarding your good works, [[6:10|and the love|et dilectionis]] of God and neighbour, [[6:10|which you have shewn|quam intus latentem, ostendistis]] outwardly by acts of charity, it being hidden within (for the showing of the work is the proof of charity: hence the Saviour also says, [[John 14:23|If any one love me, he will keep my word|Si quis diligit me, sermones meos servabit]]), [[6:10|in his name|in nomine ipsius]], that is, for the love of God and His glory; [[6:10|you who have ministered|quia ministrastis]], that is, have provided the necessaries of life and rendered fitting services, [[6:10|to the saints|sanctis]], that is, to those who are Christians in faith and deed, [[6:10|and do minister|et ministratis]] to them, persevering in the work begun: as was already said to the Galatians: [[Gal 5:13|by charity of the spirit serve one another|Per caritatem servite invicem]].

paras.t: Cupimus autem, zelo vestræ salutis accensi, unumquemque vestrum eamdem ostentare sollicitudinem, id est præmemoratam sollicitam ministrationem frequenter ostendere, ad expletionem spei, id est ad adipiscendum bonum æternum, præmiumque cœleste speratum, videlicet propter consecutionem veræ felicitatis, quæ est expletio, id est actuatio, spei : ostentare, inquam, usque in finem vitæ præsentis. Qui enim perseveraverit usque in finem, salvus erit. Ut non segnes, id est pigri ac tepidi, efficiamini : prout in Apocalypsi cuidam improperatur, Habeo adversum te quod caritatem tuam primam reliquisti ; et in eodem libro, Utinam frigidus esses aut calidus ; verum, id est sed, imitatores eorum efficiamini, qui fide et patientia, id est merito seu actibus fidei atque patientiæ, hereditabunt promissiones, id est, promissa cœlestia hereditarie possidebunt, quæ nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec cor capere valet.
paras.en: [[6:11|And we desire|Cupimus autem]], kindled with zeal for your salvation, [[6:11|that every one of you shew forth the same carefulness|unumquemque vestrum eamdem ostentare sollicitudinem]], that is, often to show the careful ministering mentioned before, [[6:11|to the accomplishing of hope|ad expletionem spei]], that is, for obtaining the eternal good and the hoped-for heavenly reward, namely for the attaining of true happiness, which is the fulfilment, that is, the actualizing, of hope: to show it, I say, [[6:11|unto the end|usque in finem]] of the present life. For [[Matt 24:13|he that shall persevere to the end, he shall be saved|Qui enim perseveraverit usque in finem, salvus erit]]. [[6:12|That you become not slothful|ut non segnes efficiamini]], that is, sluggish and lukewarm: as in the Apocalypse one is reproached, [[Apoc 2:4|I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first charity|Habeo adversum te quod caritatem tuam primam reliquisti]]; and in the same book, [[Apoc 3:15|I would thou wert cold or hot|Utinam frigidus esses aut calidus]]; [[6:12|but|verum]], that is, rather, become [[6:12|followers of them|imitatores eorum]], [[6:12|who through faith and patience|qui fide et patientia]], that is, by the merit or acts of faith and patience, [[6:12|shall inherit the promises|hereditabunt promissiones]], that is, shall possess by inheritance the heavenly things promised, which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart|nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec cor capere valet]] can contain.

paras.t: Quod autem factæ sint hominibus promissiones divinæ, consequenter ostenditur. Abrahæ namque promittens Deus bona terrena atque cœlestia, scilicet possessionem terræ Chanaan dandam semini suo, et omnes gentes benedicendas esse in semine suo, videlicet benedictione salutis æternæ, quoniam neminem, id est nullum, habuit per quem juraret, majorem : nil enim majus seu dignius est Deo, per quod possit Deus jurare ; juravit per semetipsum, dicens : Nisi benedicens benedicam te, id est, in spiritualibus ac temporalibus bonis copiam tibi præstabo : quod si non fecero, non mihi credatur, nec æstimer Deus ; et multiplicans multiplicabo te, id est, multos ex te filios procreabo. De hoc legitur in Genesi, quemadmodum Deus juraverit Abrahæ, quod semen ejus esset sicut stellæ cœli, et sicut arena maris. Et sic Abraham longanimiter ferens, id est diu patienter exspectans, adeptus est repromissionem, id est bona promissa, videlicet vitam æternam, et reliqua jam expressa.
paras.en: That divine promises were made to men is shown next. [[6:13|For God making promises to Abraham|Abrahæ namque promittens Deus]] goods earthly and heavenly, namely possession of the land of Chanaan to be given to his seed, and that all nations should be blessed in his seed, that is, with the blessing of eternal salvation[[Gen 12:1||]][[Gen 15:7||]][[Gen 15:18||]], [[6:13|because he had no one greater by whom he might swear|quoniam neminem habuit, per quem juraret, majorem]] (no one, that is, none): for nothing is greater or worthier than God, by which God could swear; [[6:13|swore by himself|juravit per semetipsum]], [[6:14|Saying: Unless blessing I shall bless thee|dicens : Nisi benedicens benedicam te]], that is, I shall give thee abundance of goods spiritual and temporal: and if I do not, let me not be believed nor reckoned God [Denis explains the Hebraic oath-formula “unless…” as an implied self-curse]; [[6:14|and multiplying I shall multiply thee|et multiplicans multiplicabo te]], that is, I shall beget many children from thee. Of this we read in Genesis, how God swore to Abraham that his seed should be as the stars of heaven and as the sand of the sea[[Gen 22:16||]][[Gen 22:17||]]. [[6:15|And so patiently enduring|Et sic Abraham longanimiter ferens]] Abraham, that is, waiting patiently a long time, [[6:15|he obtained the promise|adeptus est repromissionem]], that is, the promised goods, namely eternal life and the rest already mentioned.

paras.t: Cur autem Deus juravit, subjungitur, scilicet ad condescendendum infirmitati humanæ. Homines enim per majorem sui, id est per aliquem vere vel opinative digniorem, jurant. Confirmatio namque non fit nisi per aliquid certius atque stabilius. Idololatræ vero jurant per idola, quibus ipsi digniores sunt. Ipsi tamen idola sua deos esse putantes, arbitrantur se idolis inferiores. Et omnis controversiæ eorum finis, id est terminatio totius altercationis hominum, est juramentum, valens ad confirmationem ejus quod dicitur, cui aliter non crederetur, nisi juramento firmaretur. In quo, id est per quod juramentum Abrahæ factum, abundantius volens Deus ostendere pollicitationis suæ heredibus, id est electis divinas promissiones æternaliter possessuris, videlicet Abrahæ et semini ejus, immobilitatem consilii sui, id est invariabile propositum sapientiæ suæ, seu consilium suum immobile de salvandis. Consilium enim Dei immobile est ; et quamvis Deus mutet sententiam, non tamen consilium. Dum ergo consilium Dei juramento firmatur, multum abundanter ostenditur hominibus immobilitas divini consilii. Ideo subditur : interposuit jusjurandum, id est, sermoni quem habuit ad Abraham, miscuit juramentum, ut per duas res immobiles, id est per immobilitatem divini consilii, et infallibilitatem divini juramenti, quibus impossibile est mentiri Deum, qui est prima totius veritatis mensura, et veritas ipsa, fortissimum solatium, id est jucundam atque præcipuam securitatem sive fiduciam, habeamus de adeptione promissorum bonorum, qui confugimus ad Deum (dicentes : Domine, refugium factus es nobis), ad tenendam propositam spem, id est ad firmiter conservandam futuræ beatitudinis exspectationem.
paras.en: Why God swore is added next, namely to condescend to human weakness. [[6:16|For men swear by one greater than themselves|Homines enim per majorem sui jurant]], that is, by someone truly or reputedly worthier. For confirmation is made only by something more certain and stable. Idolaters, indeed, swear by idols, than which they themselves are worthier; yet they, thinking their idols gods, deem themselves inferior to them. [[6:16|and an oath for confirmation is the end of all their controversy|et omnis controversiæ eorum finis, ad confirmationem, est juramentum]], that is, the termination of every dispute among men, avails [[6:16|for confirmation|ad confirmationem]] of what is said, which otherwise would not be believed unless confirmed by oath. [[6:17|Wherein|In quo]], that is, by which oath made to Abraham, [[6:17|God, meaning more abundantly to shew to the heirs of the promise|abundantius volens Deus ostendere pollicitationis suæ heredibus]] (Denis reads “of *his* promise”), that is, to the elect who are to possess the divine promises eternally, namely Abraham and his seed, [[6:17|the immutability of his counsel|immobilitatem consilii sui]], that is, the unchangeable purpose of His wisdom, or His immovable counsel concerning those to be saved. For the counsel of God is immovable[[Is 46:10||]]; and although God changes His sentence, yet not His counsel. When therefore God's counsel is confirmed by oath, the immovability of the divine counsel is shown to men very abundantly. Hence it is added: [[6:17|interposed an oath|interposuit jusjurandum]], that is, He mingled an oath with the word He spoke to Abraham, [[6:18|That by two immutable things|ut per duas res immobiles]], that is, by the immovability of the divine counsel and the infallibility of the divine oath, [[6:18|in which it is impossible for God to lie|quibus impossibile est mentiri Deum]], who is the first measure of all truth and Truth itself, [[6:18|we may have the strongest comfort|fortissimum solatium habeamus]], that is, a joyful and special security or confidence about obtaining the promised goods, [[6:18|we who have fled for refuge|qui confugimus]] to God (saying: Lord, thou hast been our refuge[[Ps 89:1||]] [the margin seems to read Ps. lxxxix, 1, where the words stand]), [[6:18|to hold fast the hope set before us|ad tenendam propositam spem]], that is, to keep firmly the expectation of future beatitude.

paras.t: Quam spem sicut ancoram habemus animæ tutam ac firmam : id est, quemadmodum ancora corporalis tenet navim in fluctibus fixam, ne mergatur aut defluat, sic spes est spiritualis ancora animæ tuta et firma, id est secura et fortis, quoniam tenet animam inter prospera et adversa in Domino fixam atque illæsam. Unde in libro Machabæorum habetur : Omnes qui sperant in Domino, non infirmantur : et in Psalmo, Sperent in te qui noverunt nomen tuum, quoniam non dereliquisti quærentes te, Domine. Et incedentem, id est tendentem et nos introducentem, usque ad interiora velaminis, id est usque ad patriam Beatorum, quam modo non cernimus nisi fide, de cujus ratione est quædam obscuritas seu veritatis velamen. Interiora ergo velaminis, sunt secreta cœlestia seu beatitudo futura jam nobis velata. Inter Ecclesiam quippe militantem ac triumphantem interpositum est velamen. Ubi, id est quæ secreta patriæ, præcursor pro nobis, id est ad nostram utilitatem, introivit in ascensione, videlicet Jesus, qui exsultavit ut gigas ad currendam viam, et ante nos festinavit ad patriam, secundum ordinem Melchisedech pontifex factus in æternum. Hæc verba jam dicta sunt atque exposita.
paras.en: [[6:19|Which we have as an anchor of the soul, sure and firm|Quam spem sicut ancoram habemus animæ tutam ac firmam]]: that is, as a bodily anchor holds a ship fixed amid the waves, lest it sink or drift, so hope is the spiritual anchor of the soul, sure and firm, that is, secure and strong, since it holds the soul fixed and unharmed in the Lord amid prosperity and adversity. Hence in the book of Machabees we have: [[1 Mach 2:61|all generations: that none that trust in him, fail in strength|Omnes qui sperant in Domino, non infirmantur]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 9:11|And let them trust in thee who know thy name: for thou hast not forsaken them that seek thee|Sperent in te qui noverunt nomen tuum, quoniam non dereliquisti quærentes te, Domine]]. [[6:19|and which entereth in|Et incedentem]], that is, tending and leading us in, [[6:19|even within the veil|usque ad interiora velaminis]], that is, to the fatherland of the Blessed, which now we discern only by faith, to whose nature belongs a certain obscurity or veil of truth. The things within the veil, then, are the heavenly secrets, or the future beatitude now veiled from us. For between the Church militant and triumphant a veil is set. [[6:20|Where|Ubi]], that is, into which secrets of the fatherland, [[6:20|the forerunner Jesus is entered for us|præcursor pro nobis]], that is, for our profit, [[6:20|is entered|introivit]] at the Ascension, namely [[6:20|Jesus|Jesus]], who [[Ps 18:6|Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way|exsultavit ut gigas ad currendam viam]], and hastened before us to the fatherland, [[6:20|according to the order of Melchisedech|secundum ordinem Melchisedech pontifex factus in æternum]][[Ps 109:4||]]. These words have already been spoken and expounded.
